title: Charging by the Second: Globacom's Late Entry Into Nigeria, 2003
conflicts: 2001 licence: RCR Wireless (2001) gives a $285m fee due in 14 days, not deposited, and contested; ThisDay (2023) gives a $265m balance after a $20m deposit missed 'by a few hours'; ThisDay (2022) dates a conditional licence to 1999. Story uses RCR and attributes the lost deposit to ThisDay. Line prices (N6,000 in the 2004 cable vs N6,999 in ThisDay 2022) and early subscriber counts (600,000 in six months per the cable vs over a million in nine months per ThisDay) differ; story uses the cable and omits line prices.
notes: No Adenuga interview used; strategy is attributed to Glo executives as paraphrased in a 2004 US consulate cable (WikiLeaks, via Scoop). Nigerian anniversary/tribute pieces used only for widely reported facts. Funding changed from the slate's 'bootstrapped' to 'unknown': privately held, Adenuga widely believed to be sole financier (TechCabal), but financing of the $1.2bn rollout is undocumented. The story ends with Glo's 2024 subscriber recount and change of management, told factually.
